title: PRD: Adaptive Micro‑Endpoints for Hosted Inference — Traffic Slicing, Behavioral SLAs & Launch Runbook
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Context:
Redwood hosted customers want a predictable, low-cost path to surface narrow inference capabilities (chat, completion, embeddings, rerank) as small, composable micro-endpoints. Current monolithic endpoint bundles increase cost and complicate routing and SLA guarantees. This PRD defines Adaptive Micro-Endpoints: lightweight hosted endpoints that can be traffic-sliced by intent, latency tier, and cost tier while preserving behavioral contracts and operational guardrails.

Objective:
- Define product surface and API contract for Micro-Endpoints (ME) that support chat/completions/embeddings/rerank as first-class, composable operations.
- Provide traffic-slicing primitives (intent tags, weight rules, latency tiers) so customers can route specific intents to specialized models/variants.
- Ship acceptance criteria, telemetry, and a launch runbook enabling canary → regional rollout with automated fallback policies.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing Dedicated capacity billing or Reserved capacity primitives.
- Not introducing new model training/eval tooling; relies on existing eval infra.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Avery Chen (owner)
- Eng leads: Rohit Malhotra (API), Laila Torres (runtime), Mateo Silva (console)
- Design: Priya Kapoor

Product requirements (high level):
1) API surface and contract:
   - New micro-endpoint resource: POST /v1/micro_endpoints with JSON spec to declare: intents (list), allowed operations (chat/completion/embedding/rerank), model variants, latency_tier (low|standard|high), cost_tier (eco|balanced|premium), and routing_weights.
   - Requests include an "intent" field or auto-intent inference hook (optional). If missing, default route applies.
   - Response semantics identical to existing endpoints (streaming support for chat/completions, batch and async for embeddings). Documented backward-compatible behaviors.

2) Traffic slicing and routing primitives:
   - Intent-based routing: evaluate request.intent first; match to configured micro-endpoint; then apply weight rules.
   - Weighted split and percentage pins per micro-endpoint.
   - Tiered latency policy: enforce target p50/p95 thresholds per latency_tier with SLA labels surfaced in Console.

3) Behavioral SLAs and fallbacks:
   - Define behavioral SLA matrix per operation (e.g., chat p50<=60ms, p95<=200ms for low-latency tier).
   - Auto-fallback: if configured model variant exceeds error or latency thresholds for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows, route to fallback variant (configurable).

4) Observability + Console:
   - Per-micro-endpoint dashboard: traffic split, latency p50/p95, error rates, cost per token, token distribution by intent.
   - Canary view showing canary vs baseline performance and quality deltas (paired with eval signal when available).

5) Access control and isolation:
   - Micro-endpoints inherit workspace-level RBAC. Private deployments: support VPC-scoped micro-endpoints and audit log entries for routing changes.

Acceptance criteria (must pass all):
- API contract validated: Create/update/delete micro-endpoints via API and Console; spec is schema-validated.
- Intent routing correctness: Given synthetic traffic with labelled intents, routing matches configured micro-endpoint and respects weight rules in >99.5% of requests over 24-hour test.
- Latency tier guarantees: Under representative load profile (defined below), p50/p95 targets for each latency_tier are met in 95% of test windows and never regressed vs baseline by >15%.
- Auto-fallback functions: Induce high latency/error on primary variant and validate automatic switching to fallback within configured windows, with telemetry showing the switch.
- Streaming parity: chat/completion streaming behaves identically to existing endpoints (no protocol regressions).
- Billing and metrics: token accounting and cost-per-token surfaced in Console match backend billing within 1% for test workloads.
- Security review sign-off: security_review_required completed and documented.
- E2E rollout runbook executed in internal staging with canary traffic and postmortem logged.

Minimum viable launch scope:
- Support for intents + weighted routing for chat and completions. Embeddings and rerank supported in MVP as non-streaming (sync) operations.
- One low-latency tier and one standard tier. Eco and premium cost_tiers optional (beta).
- Console dashboard for per-micro-endpoint basics (traffic, latency, errors, cost).

Launch checklist (operational tasks):
- API & Console:
  - [ ] API schema implemented and unit-tested (ENG).
  - [ ] Console UI for creating micro-endpoint SSH (UX + ENG).
  - [ ] Patch release notes and API migration guide (Docs).

- Runtime & SRE:
  - [ ] Routing engine supports weighted intent routing for ME (ENG).
  - [ ] Auto-fallback engine with configurable windows (ENG + SRE).
  - [ ] Load testing: run 3 sustained 2-hour stress runs covering 50/90/99th percentile token lengths. Record latencies. (SRE)
  - [ ] Chaos test: simulate region failover and verify fallback routing and SLA preservation.

- Quality & Telemetry:
  - [ ] Eval harness: run a curated prompt set (per-intent) to detect behavioral regressions for each model variant.
  - [ ] Dashboard: per-ME p50/p95, error rate, cost/token, traffic split.
  - [ ] Alerts: p95 > target OR error_rate > 1% triggers paged alert.

- Security & Compliance:
  - [ ] KMS key usage documented for Private deployments.
  - [ ] Audit log entries for create/update/delete actions enabled.
  - [ ] Security review completed and findings remediated.

- Release & Rollout:
  - [ ] Internal staging rollout complete with customer-proxy traffic.
  - [ ] Canary 1: 1% of production traffic for 24h, monitor metrics and quality; hold if behavioral regressions > threshold.
  - [ ] Canary 2: 10% for 48h, monitor support chatter and model quality.
  - [ ] Regional ramp: 25% → 50% → 100% over 7 days with automated rollback on SLA breach.

Telemetry test profile (for QA runs):
- Synthetic workload A: small chat messages, average 20 tokens, QPS 200 across intents: 60% intent-A, 30% intent-B, 10% default.
- Synthetic workload B: embeddings batch size 64, throughput 50/s for a 2 hour window.
- Latency noise injection: add 150ms tail noise to one variant to validate fallback and alerting.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Intent inference auto-hook: postpone auto-intent inference to post-MVP due to classifier drift concerns. For MVP, require explicit intent field or opt-in inference flag.
- Number of tiers: start with 2 latency tiers to reduce complexity; expand after observed demand.
- Billing model: weight usage to existing token billing; consider per-endpoint surcharge for premium tiers in a later release.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Intent misclassification leads to poor routing → mitigation: require explicit intents for initial beta and robust analytics to detect misroutes.
- Risk: Tier guarantees may increase infra costs → mitigation: tiered autoscaling policies and conservative default scaling.
- Risk: Behavioral regressions across model variants → mitigation: eval guardrails and paired A/B evaluation hooks before full rollout.

- Cost efficiency: average cost/token for eco tier <= baseline -10% for targeted intents.
- Reliability: p95 latency within SLA in >= 99% of 1-hour windows.
- Quality: eval regression alerts for new endpoints <= 2 per 10k requests.
